issues.title: Boundary-incompatible continuous T-operator

failure_location.quote: Let $u \in X$ be arbitrary and $u^{(i)} \in \mathbb{C}$ s.t. $u = \sum_{i \in \mathbb{N}} u^{(i)} e^{(i)}$.

issues.failure_explanation: For the sound-hard branch, X=H^2(Omega) contains the constant function, whereas every old auxiliary eigenfunction lies in H^2(Omega) intersect H^1_0(Omega). An L^2 expansion in those functions does not supply the X-convergent, energy-diagonal expansion used in the proof. More decisively, the old energy projection leaves the constant mode unchanged, so T1=1 and the negative mass term makes the asserted coercivity inequality fail. The sound-soft spectrum also cannot justify the hard nonresonance invocation.
issues.overall_effect: Continuous T-coercivity for the non-soft boundary spaces, the corresponding hard nonresonance argument, and the later transfer of stability to impedance discretizations are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the universal sound-soft auxiliary problem by a self-adjoint generalized eigenproblem posed on the actual continuous energy space for each boundary condition. Prove spectral completeness in an equivalent H² norm, include the hard zero/constant mode and all other missing boundary modes, define T by flipping every eigenmode with eigenvalue below k², and use that same boundary-compatible spectrum in the nonresonance, injectivity, and dependent stability statements.
issues.why_classification: The old expansion is invalid and the resulting T is noncoercive even on the constant function, so this is not a transcription error. Repair requires a new boundary-compatible spectral lemma, treatment of the kernel, and propagation of the corrected spectrum, but it remains within the existing T-coercivity architecture and preserves the same nonresonant well-posedness and approximation guarantees.

issues.title: Undefined second-derivative traces in the continuous boundary perturbation

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For impedance boundary conditions, we set $X \coloneqq H^2(\Omega)$

issues.failure_explanation: For u in H^2(Omega), Delta u and n^T H(u)n are only L^2(Omega) quantities and have no bounded ordinary boundary trace. Nevertheless, the old boundary forms and compactness proof apply gamma_0 to them and use L^2(partial Omega) pairings. Thus the associated operator and K are not established as bounded operators on X, so K cannot be asserted to be compact.
issues.overall_effect: The old compact-perturbation and Fredholm chain is unavailable for the sound-hard form as written and for the continuous impedance formulation. In particular, continuous impedance well-posedness and downstream impedance quasi-optimality do not follow.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For sound-hard conditions, work on X_hard={u∈H²(Ω): ∂νu=0} and use the trace-free volume form, so that no such boundary perturbation is needed. On the least-burden complete route, remove the continuous impedance formulation and restrict every listed Fredholm, well-posedness, consistency, and quasi-optimality result to the sound-soft and sound-hard branches; impedance computations must be presented without those guarantees.
issues.why_classification: The offending traces do not define bounded operators on H², and additional regularity of the exact solution alone cannot make the variational operator bounded on its trial and test space. Although the hard branch has a local bypass, withdrawing the advertised impedance theory and its convergence result is major mathematical loss. Retaining that branch requires a mixed, graph-space, or Petrov–Galerkin formulation and reconstruction of the well-posedness and approximation chain, so no complete moderate route is established.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Unfortunately, this term is not bounded on $H^2(\Omega) \times H^2(\Omega)$

issues.title: Invalid cancellation argument for impedance injectivity

failure_location.quote: which implies that $\gamma_0 v = 0$ and $\gamma_0 \Delta v = 0$ on $\partial \Omega$

issues.failure_explanation: Young's inequality supplies an upper bound for the magnitude of the cross term; it does not imply that the absolute value of a positive boundary norm minus that cross term dominates a positive sum of the two squared norms. The two terms can cancel. Therefore the proof cannot infer that both v and Delta v vanish on the boundary, and the subsequent zero extension and unique-continuation argument lacks its required premise.
issues.overall_effect: Impedance injectivity, the Fredholm conclusion requiring it, and the downstream impedance stability and quasi-optimality claims remain unproved independently of the separate trace-definition problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false Young-inequality step by a genuine impedance uniqueness argument. For β=0 and positive dissipative impedance, factor αΔ²−Δ−k² as α(Δ−r₊)(Δ−r₋); because both v and Δv satisfy the same Robin condition, the corresponding factor inherits that condition, and standard energy and unique-continuation arguments successively force both factors and v to vanish. For sufficiently small β, establish injectivity by bounded perturbation from the β=0 impedance operator, and then reuse it in the Fredholm and downstream stability arguments.
issues.why_classification: The displayed lower bound cannot be repaired algebraically, but a contained replacement proof exists through factorization, Robin uniqueness, and small-β perturbation. This is a nontrivial new uniqueness argument rather than a routine local edit, while it preserves the impedance model and the dependent guarantees without global proof reconstruction.

issues.title: Nonsymmetric continuous nematic eigenproblem

failure_location.quote: Due to the regularity of the functions $u, v \in H^2_0(\Omega)$, we can swap the order of differentiation and integrate by parts to show that the last two terms in \eqref{eq:exp} are self-adjoint as well.

issues.failure_explanation: An admissible counterexample is Omega=(0,pi)^2, n=(1,1)/sqrt(2), u=sin(x)sin(y), and v=sin(2x)sin(2y). Both functions lie in the old H^2(Omega) intersect H^1_0(Omega) space, but for B(u,v)=(n^T H(u)n,Delta v), one obtains B(u,v)=-128/9 and B(v,u)=-32/9. Thus the nematic form is not symmetric; the stated boundary regularity does not remove the boundary terms needed by the integration-by-parts argument. The mixed-derivative coefficient in the displayed expansion is also not the coefficient obtained by expanding Delta(n^T H(u)n).
issues.overall_effect: The claimed real eigenvalues and orthogonal eigenbasis are unjustified, so the beta-dependent continuous T construction and the inherited beta-dependent spectral index used later are unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Let D_nn u=nᵀH(u)n and replace the auxiliary nematic eigenform by its Hermitian part, with cross term β[(D_nn u,Δv)+(Δu,D_nn v)]/2. Prove coercivity for small β and the resulting compact self-adjoint spectral decomposition, construct T from that real spectrum, and treat the skew-Hermitian remainder of the physical form as an O(β) bounded perturbation. Remove or correct the invalid differential expansion and propagate the corrected spectral index and nonresonance condition through the dependent results.
issues.why_classification: The old nematic form is genuinely nonsymmetric, so its claimed real orthogonal spectral basis cannot be recovered by a notation correction. A comparable β-dependent auxiliary spectral result and the same well-posedness chain can nevertheless be retained through a contained symmetrization and perturbation argument. That requires a new spectral construction and absorption estimate but not global architecture or major loss.

issues.title: Discrete impedance eigenbasis does not span the trial space

failure_location.quote: For any $u_h \in X_h$, we have that due to the smallness assumption on $h$

issues.failure_explanation: With epsilon=0, the old text places the auxiliary eigenproblem on a space contained in H^1_0(Omega), whereas the impedance discrete problem is posed on all of X_h. The constant finite element function belongs to X_h but not to the auxiliary space, so the auxiliary eigenfunctions cannot form the X_h basis assumed by the spectral sum. The old T_h leaves this missing constant direction untreated, and the negative mass term prevents coercivity there. The imposed auxiliary conditions also do not encode the advertised Robin interface.
issues.overall_effect: The impedance branch of the old discrete T_h-coercivity theorem, and both later best-approximation conclusions insofar as they cover impedance conditions, are unsupported. The sound-soft branch is not affected by this root.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Pose the auxiliary impedance eigenproblem on the entire trial space X_h, using the same Robin/Nitsche boundary treatment as the impedance discretization rather than homogeneous Dirichlet restrictions. Prove the associated symmetric energy plus mass defines a uniform norm and supplies a complete X_h eigenbasis, include the constant and all other boundary modes among the eigenvectors, flip every eigenmode below k², and redo the uniform T_h-coercivity and dependent best-approximation arguments.
issues.why_classification: The old spectral sum omits genuine trial-space directions and fails on the constant function, so the proof cannot be fixed by changing an index. Constructing and analyzing a full-space auxiliary eigenproblem is nontrivial, but it is a contained replacement within the existing discrete T_h framework and preserves the impedance method and its intended guarantees.

issues.title: Missing trace regularity for Galerkin consistency
issues.failure_explanation: For a generic H^2 solution, nabla(Delta u)·nu and, in the nematic case, nabla(n^T H(u)n)·nu have no L^2 boundary trace. Consequently a_h(u,v_h), the asserted partial integration, and the old mesh-dependent norm of u-v_h are not defined under the corollary's stated hypothesis. The old paper therefore claims consistency for more solutions than its formulas can accommodate.
issues.overall_effect: Galerkin orthogonality and both best-approximation chains are established only after imposing additional trace regularity; they do not hold as stated for every H^2 solution.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State Galerkin orthogonality and the dependent best-approximation theorems only for solutions in an extended regularity space where the required boundary traces exist—for example, with ∇(Δu)·ν and ∇(D_nn u)·ν in L²(∂Ω), together with the lower-order traces needed by the relevant boundary branch. Define the mesh-dependent norm on that extended space and then carry out the same integration-by-parts and quasi-optimality proof.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine missing premise because the old formulas are undefined for a generic H² solution. Adding the standard trace-regularity hypothesis is short and local, and it leaves the discretization, consistency identity, quasi-optimal conclusion, and approximation rate unchanged in the intended regular-solution regime; no new construction or substantial proof is required.

issues.title: Nonsymmetric discrete nematic eigenproblem

failure_location.quote: the proof follows with exactly the same argument as in the proof of \cref{thm:DiscreteThCoercivity}

issues.failure_explanation: On Omega=(0,1)^2 with n=(1,0), the global polynomials u_h=x^2 and v_h=y^2 belong to the stated finite element space. The nematic volume pairing equals 4 in the order (u_h,v_h) and 0 in the reverse order, while the nematic boundary symmetry terms vanish because the relevant second derivatives are constant. Hence e_h is not symmetric. Uniform coercivity alone does not provide the ordered real orthogonal eigenbasis used to define T_h, so the claim cannot follow by exactly the symmetric-case argument.
issues.overall_effect: Uniform discrete T_h-coercivity for the nematic problem and its ensuing beta-dependent best-approximation theorem are not established by the old spectral construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Do not obtain T_h from the nonsymmetric β-dependent eigenproblem. Construct it from the symmetric β=0 discrete eigenproblem on the same full trial space, prove the resulting projections and spectral gap are uniform, and bound all β-dependent volume and boundary terms by the discrete norm using the inverse-trace estimates. Choose β sufficiently small and the stabilization parameters sufficiently large to absorb those perturbations, then propagate the corrected T_h-coercivity to the β-dependent best-approximation theorem.
issues.why_classification: Uniform coercivity of the nonsymmetric form does not supply the ordered real orthogonal eigenbasis used in the old proof. The theorem and its approximation guarantee can be recovered without changing the method or rate, but doing so requires a replacement spectral construction and a uniform perturbation and stabilization argument, which exceeds a minor local repair while remaining contained.
